scenes.title: Rooftop chase (text-to-video, action-heavy)
scenes.idea: A woman in a red raincoat sprints along a rain-soaked rooftop at dusk, leaps a two-metre gap onto the next roof, lands in a roll and keeps running; the camera tracks alongside her at speed, rain streaking past the lens, city lights blurring behind.
scenes.why: Pure text-to-video with several sequential action beats (sprint, leap, roll, run). The hardest test of action adherence and motion: a weak prompt tends to drop or merge beats, which is exactly what the arm comparison is about.

scenes.title: Kitchen confession (dialogue, audio-heavy)
scenes.idea: At a dim kitchen table at night, a tired paramedic in a damp jacket looks up and says quietly, "I called her. She knows now." The fridge hums and rain taps the window behind her; she lowers her head into her hands.
scenes.why: Spoken line plus diegetic sound: the only scene where the audio criterion can separate the arms, and lip-sync/speech is where raw idea text most often loses structure.

scenes.title: The same mug (image-referenced identity)
scenes.idea: A hand reaches in and lifts the ceramic mug from [Picture 1] off the counter, turns it slowly so the printed label stays readable, and sets it back down; the camera holds on the mug the whole time with shallow depth of field.
scenes.why: Image-referenced generation: identity means the mug (label, shape, colour) survives being handled and stays recognizable. Portable by default; if the user supplies a private portrait photo (PILOT_PORTRAIT_IMAGE) it rides along as a second reference and identity also covers the person - equally for both arms.
